activities.anchor: That single line hides two linked stages
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the engine's two stages
activities.name: pbStagesCloze

config.text: In the %%0%% stage, chlorophyll in the thylakoid membranes splits %%1%% — liberating the oxygen and charging ATP and NADPH. In the %%2%% %%3%%, those carriers power the fixation of CO₂ until glucose emerges. Chlorophyll absorbs %%4%% light strongly and reflects green.
config.hint: The Calvin cycle needs no light itself — but it cannot run for long without the carriers.

activities.caption: true or false — day and night chemistry
activities.name: pbRespireJudge

statements.s: Respiration never stops — every living plant cell burns sugar for energy around the clock.
statements.why: Photosynthesis simply adds on top in the light.

statements.s: By day a leaf photosynthesises and respires at once.
statements.why: Two processes, one leaf — photosynthesis usually out-earns the spending in daylight.

statements.s: Plants photosynthesise by day and respire only at night.
statements.why: The classic misconception — respiration runs day and night like any tissue's.

statements.s: At night a plant keeps respiring like any other tissue.
statements.why: Which is why a sealed bedroom full of houseplants is undramatically harmless.

activities.anchor: CO₂ can only enter through open pores
activities.caption: the leaf's trade-off — drag from open to closed
activities.name: pbPoresCompare

config.prompt: The stomatal bargain — drag the divider across the guard cells:

before.label: pores open
before.text: CO₂ enters for photosynthesis — and water vapour leaks out. The intake vents are also the main leak.

after.label: pores closed
after.text: Guard cells slack under drought stress and close the pore — the gas trade stops, but so does the leak. Wilting is the emergency measure.

config.why: Which is why desert plants open stomata only at night — CAM photosynthesis stores the CO₂ as an acid until daylight.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — a tree's source of mass
activities.name: pbMassEstimate

config.prompt: Van Helmont's willow gained 74 kg while 90 kg of soil barely changed. About what percentage of a tree's dry mass is carbon pulled from the air as CO₂?
config.why: About 95%, plus water from the soil — forests are solidified atmosphere.
config.context: The truth is more extreme than even van Helmont's conclusion; he guessed water, and CO₂ was still unknown.

activities.caption: pair each root job with its mechanism
activities.name: pbRootMatch

config.prompt: The hidden half at work — pair each job with its mechanism:

pairs.right: active transport against gradients, billed in ATP
passive osmosis, drawn in by ion-rich root cells
thousands of root hairs behind the growing tip
mycorrhizal fungi trading phosphorus for sugar

config.why: Roughly 90% of plant species run the fungal partnership, and the oldest fossil plants show it — as old as land plants themselves.

activities.anchor: hauled up by evaporation at the top
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the xylem answer
activities.name: pbXylemSpot

config.prompt: This water-transport answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Xylem — dead, hollow, lignified tubes — carries water and minerals upward from root to leaf.
Its engine is cohesion–tension: transpiration from the leaf pulls the water column from the top.
Hydrogen bonding makes water cohesive enough to behave like a rope under tension.
A large tree moves hundreds of litres a day to heights over 100 metres, with zero moving parts.
The engine sits in the roots, which pump water up under pressure from below.
config.correction: The engine sits at the TOP — evaporation pulls the column; roots supply the water but do not pump it.
config.why: The proof is in the failure mode: the columns are under tension from above, and an air bubble breaking the chain stops transport dead, however healthy the roots.

config.prompt: Phloem sap flows from source to sink under pressure — aphids tapping it drink pressurised sugar solution. Roughly how fast does phloem sap move in trees?
config.why: Around 1 metre per hour, driven by pressure differences of only a few atmospheres — respectable, for plumbing with no pump.
config.context: Xylem tension at the top of tall trees reaches roughly −2 to −4 MPa, approaching the tensile limit of water itself.

activities.anchor: each hormone is a word in that language
activities.caption: prescribe the hormone — run the switchboard
activities.name: pbHormoneBranch

config.root: With no nerves, plants steer with chemistry: five hormones, each a word in the language. Pick the right one for the job.

choices.label: Bend the shoot toward the light
choices.feedback: Auxin migrates to the shaded side, which then grows faster.

choices.label: Awaken the embryo and mobilise starch reserves
Close the stomata in a drought
Ripen the fruit — and warn the neighbours

auxin.text: Phototropism. The same chemical in roots accumulates on the lower side and INHIBITS elongation — gravitropism bends roots down.

gibb.text: Gibberellins also drive stem elongation — the Green Revolution's dwarf wheat carried mutations in gibberellin genes.

aba.text: Abscisic acid — stress hormone and seed-dormancy enforcer. Cytokinins, meanwhile, promote cell division and delay leaf ageing.

ethylene.text: One over-ripening fruit ethylene-bombs the barrel — and green bananas ripen in a sealed bag.

config.why: Synthetic auxins are selective weedkillers (2,4-D distorts broadleaf weeds, grasses barely respond); rooting powders are auxin — plant pharmacy and agriculture at once.
